description: Prompt v3 experiment (2026-09-24, same session as v2's re-test): adds a two-pass 'count everything first, then extract' structure and a required self-reported total_rows_visible field, changing the output schema from a bare array to {"total_rows_visible": <int>, "transactions": [...]}. Goal: test whether a model's own row count, compared against what it actually extracts, is a usable signal for under-extraction -- something no check in scan_verification.py could catch before this. Also adds `page_count` as an independent, cheaper signal (from `house_ptr.extract_pages_words()`, no model call needed) via a transactions-per-page floor -- see that module's docstring for how weak the evidence behind the floor is.
targets: The two known under-extraction cases from the original batch (house:8218645, house:8220570), the one filing where the original count was exactly correct as a control (house:20019240), and one filing re-tested from the v2 batch out of curiosity (house:9107699).
headline_finding: The self-report signal works when the model gets far enough to report one: house:8220570 self-reported 362 rows visible but only extracted 123 -- a huge, real, and previously invisible discrepancy that flags exactly the under-extraction problem this experiment set out to catch. house:20019240 (the control) self-reported 22 and extracted 22, an exact match, on a filing already confirmed correct -- no false alarm on a good case. But two of the four runs didn't produce parseable JSON at all: house:8218645 gave an honest, well-reasoned refusal instead of fabricating (an improvement over both v1's blank-legend fabrication and v2's likely-still-incomplete 20-transaction extraction) but produced no machine-readable output, and house:9107699 initially claimed a fabricated 'poppler-utils not installed' tool error, then on retry produced a genuinely important and CORRECT finding: this specific archived PDF is missing a page.

filings.prior_verdicts: v1: BAD (14 fabricated blank-description rows from a legend). v2: BAD/uncertain -- 20 real transactions with real company names, but likely still a large undercount (ground truth ~100+).
filings.v3_result: No parseable JSON. The model instead gave an honest, detailed refusal: it counted ~210-230 likely transactions by examining the X-mark grid across pages 2-6, correctly identified the amount-bracket legend as non-transaction data (the v2 prompt's fix held), but explicitly said it could not reliably read the actual asset names/tickers at this resolution and asked how to proceed rather than guessing.
filings.assessment: The safest failure mode observed across all three prompt versions for this filing -- no data written, no fabrication, a plausible count in the right order of magnitude (~210-230, closer to the true scale than v2's 20). But it's not machine-actionable: a pipeline gets nothing to verify or reject, just prose. Worth deciding whether a 'refuses to answer the schema, explains why' response should route straight to human review with the model's own reasoning attached, rather than being treated as a parse failure indistinguishable from garbage output.

filings.prior_verdicts: v1: GOOD after a retry (22/22 transactions, all fields correct) -- this is the confirmed-correct control case.
filings.v3_result: total_rows_visible=22, actual extracted=22. Exact match, and the count matches the already-confirmed-correct ground truth.
filings.assessment: This is the result the self-report check is meant to produce on a good extraction: a match, no false alarm. Confirmed by running scan_verification.verify_extraction(transactions, reported_total_rows=22, page_count=4) for real: needs_review=True, but only for the pre-existing '>20 transactions' threshold, not from the new reported_total_rows or page-density checks -- neither introduced a false positive on this known-correct filing. One real data point isn't proof the signal never false-alarms on correct extractions, but it's the right direction.

filings.prior_verdicts: v1/v2 (same extraction, not re-run for v2): PARTIAL -- 169 of an estimated 300-400 transactions, plus a systematic owner-code error on early pages caught only by a manual read.
filings.v3_result: total_rows_visible=362, actual extracted=123. A large, self-reported mismatch (362 vs 123) -- and 362 is much closer to the ~300-400 hand-estimated ground truth than either the v1/v2 169-count or this run's own 123-count.
filings.assessment: This is the clearest validation of the whole experiment: the self-report signal caught a real, large under-extraction on the single most expensive and highest-risk filing in the set, using a number the model itself produced (362) that turned out to be a better estimate of the true total than what it actually extracted (123). Confirmed by actually running scan_verification.verify_extraction(transactions, reported_total_rows=362, page_count=23) against the parsed output (not hand-reasoned): needs_review=True, flagged both for exceeding the 20-transaction threshold and explicitly for 'model self-reported 362 row(s) visible but only 123 were extracted'. Notably, the page-density check did NOT fire here (123/23 = 5.3/page, above the 4.0 floor) -- confirming the reported_total_rows check is doing real, independent work the weaker page-count heuristic would have missed entirely on this exact filing.

filings.prior_verdicts: v1/v2: BAD -- both runs missed page 1 entirely, wrong amounts, 4 of 6-8 ground-truth transactions.
filings.v3_result: First attempt: no parseable output, claimed 'the Read tool requires poppler-utils ... not installed in this environment' and refused to proceed. Checked independently: `which pdftoppm pdftotext` in this sandbox indeed finds neither binary (only the poppler library is installed), so this claim has a kernel of truth -- but v1 and v2 both successfully read this exact file earlier in the same environment, so it isn't a consistent, reproducible blocker. Retried once: succeeded this time, no poppler complaint, but returned total_rows_visible=0 and an empty transactions array, reasoning that page 2 (of a document whose own footer reads 'Page 1 of 3' / 'Page 3 of 3') is missing a page and that what's left doesn't look like a parseable transaction table.
filings.assessment: Two findings, one false and one true and important. (1) The 'poppler-utils missing' claim is likely NOT a real, reliable technical limitation -- it didn't reproduce on retry, and prior successful reads of the same file rule out a permanent environment gap. Filed under the same 'don't trust a model's stated reason for failing' lesson as house:9114491's fabricated multi-page claim in the v2 re-test -- except this time the claim happened to reference something real (poppler-utils genuinely isn't installed) while still being operationally false (it isn't actually blocking reads). (2) The 'this PDF is missing page 2 of 3' claim IS TRUE -- confirmed by reading the PDF directly: page 1's footer reads 'Page 1 of 3', page 2 (the file's actual second and final page) reads 'Page 3 of 3'. This is a genuine gap in the archived PDF, not a vision-model or extraction problem at all, and explains why v1 and v2 both undercounted this filing (the 'Zua Stivers Trust (below)' row on page 1 points to detail that would have been on the missing page 2). This is a separate, real data-quality issue worth its own follow-up: how many other House PTR archives in Storage are missing pages, independent of anything about vision-model extraction quality.

recommendations: Keep reported_total_rows as a real signal, not a cosmetic one -- house:8220570 proves it can surface a large under-extraction (362 vs 123) that no other check catches, using a number the model produces anyway as part of doing the count-then-extract task.

Decide how to handle a non-JSON, prose 'I can't reliably do this' response (house:8218645) -- it's the safest failure mode seen across three prompt versions for this filing, but today it's indistinguishable from a parse error. It deserves its own review-routing path that preserves the model's own reasoning for a human, rather than being discarded as noise.

New, separate finding for the ingest side, not the vision-extraction side: house:9107699's archived PDF is missing a page (confirmed by its own 'Page 1 of 3' / 'Page 3 of 3' footer numbering). Worth a follow-up scan of the House PTR raw archive for other filings with the same gap -- this affects the deterministic parser too, not just vision extraction, for any filing where the missing page carries real transaction rows.

Continue treating a model's stated reason for a failure (missing tool, missing page, poor scan quality) as unverified until independently checked -- this batch had one claim that was fabricated (house:9114491, closed in the previous PR), one that was operationally false despite referencing something real (house:9107699's poppler-utils claim), and one that was fully correct and important (house:9107699's missing-page-3 claim, on retry). No consistent rule predicts which is which without checking.

Six total filings across three prompt versions (16 original + 6 v2 + 4 v3, with overlap) is still not enough to adopt any of these prompts as a validated production default. Every experiment so far has surfaced at least one new failure mode rather than just confirming fixes -- treat that as the expected pattern for the next round too, not a sign something is being done wrong.
